john-of-gischala.s: John of Gischala was a leader of the First Jewish–Roman War from the town of Gischala in Galilee. After Vespasian took Galilee he escaped to Jerusalem, where he joined the Zealots and fought rival factions under Simon bar Giora and Eleazar ben Simon.

john-of-islay.n: John of Islay, Lord of the Isles
john-of-islay.s: John of Islay was a chief of Clan Donald, descended from Somerled, who was the first to style himself Lord of the Isles (Dominus Insularum). Through marriages to Amy MacRuari and to a daughter of Robert II of Scotland he built a Gaelic lordship spanning the Hebrides and the…

john-duke-of-brunswick-luneburg.s: John, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, was a son of Otto the Child. When he and his brother Albert the Tall divided the duchy in 1269, John received Lüneburg and became the first prince of the Principality of Lüneburg.

john-of-montfort.s: John of Montfort was lord of Tyre in the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem from 1270, succeeding his father Philip of Montfort, who was murdered by an Assassin. He kept the city's trade alive through truces with the Mamluk sultans.

john-of-neuilly.s: John of Neuilly was a Frankish knight and hereditary marshal of the Principality of Achaea. Around 1220 he received a fief at the entrance to the Mani peninsula in the Peloponnese and built the castle of Passavant to control the Maniots.

john-penn-governor.s: John Penn was a grandson of William Penn and a proprietor of Pennsylvania. He served as lieutenant governor of the Province of Pennsylvania and of the Lower Counties on Delaware from 1763 to 1771 and again from 1773 to 1776, making him the last colonial governor before the…

john-sevier.s: John Sevier was a frontier soldier and politician who fought at the Battle of Kings Mountain in 1780. He served as governor of the breakaway State of Franklin from 1785 until it collapsed in 1788.

john-smith-explorer.s: John Smith was an English soldier and explorer who helped found Jamestown in 1607 and led the Virginia colony as president of its council in 1608 and 1609. His leadership kept the struggling settlement alive through its early hardships.

john-smith-missionary.s: John Smith was an English missionary of the London Missionary Society who served enslaved people in Demerara from 1817. After the Demerara rebellion of 1823 he was accused of encouraging the rising, court-martialled and sentenced to death, and died in prison in 1824 before a…

john-vii-count-of-nassau-siegen.s: John VII, Count of Nassau-Siegen, known as John the Middle, received Siegen after the death of his father, John VI of Nassau-Dillenburg, in 1606. A leading Calvinist military reformer, he wrote on the drill methods of the Dutch army and founded a military academy at Siegen in…

john-viii-count-of-nassau-siegen.s: John VIII, Count of Nassau-Siegen, known as John the Younger, was a son of John VII. He converted to Catholicism in 1612 and served Spain as a general.

john-wentworth-governor.s: John Wentworth was the last royal governor of the Province of New Hampshire, appointed in 1767 in succession to his uncle Benning Wentworth. He granted the charter of Dartmouth College in 1769 and built roads, but fled in 1775 as the American Revolution began.

john-william-friso.s: John William Friso was prince of Nassau-Dietz and stadtholder of Friesland and Groningen. In 1702 he inherited part of William III's estate and took the title Prince of Orange, though the inheritance was disputed with Prussia.

john-winthrop.s: John Winthrop was an English Puritan lawyer who led the Winthrop Fleet of about 1,000 settlers to Massachusetts in 1630 and founded Boston. Governor of the Massachusetts Bay Colony for most of its first two decades, he described the colony as a 'city upon a hill'.

jon-sigurdsson.s: Jón Sigurðsson was an Icelandic scholar and politician who led the nineteenth-century movement for Iceland's self-government from Copenhagen. As president of the Althing he pressed Denmark for home rule, and the constitution of 1874 granted Iceland control over its own affairs.

jonathan-trumbull.s: Jonathan Trumbull was governor of the Connecticut Colony from 1769 to 1784 and the only colonial governor to support the American Revolution. Under him Connecticut kept its charter government and supplied the Continental Army with food, cattle and munitions, earning the name…

jonker-afrikaner.s: Jonker Afrikaner was the leader of the Oorlam Afrikaners, a horse-riding, gun-using community from the Cape frontier. Around 1823 he moved north into central Namibia at the invitation of the Nama to fight the Herero, and by about 1840 settled at Windhoek.

jorge-de-figueiredo-correia.s: Jorge de Figueiredo Correia was a Portuguese royal official and treasury scribe to whom King John III granted the Captaincy of Ilhéus in Brazil in 1534. He never went to the colony, governing through his lieutenant Francisco Romero, who founded the town of São Jorge dos Ilhéus.

jose-antonio-aguirre.s: José Antonio Aguirre was a Basque Nationalist Party politician and former footballer who became the first lehendakari, or president, of the autonomous Basque government. He took his oath under the oak of Guernica on 7 October 1936, during the Spanish Civil War.

jose-de-anchieta.s: José de Anchieta was a Spanish-born Jesuit missionary from Tenerife who worked in Brazil from 1553. With Manuel da Nóbrega he founded the mission that became São Paulo in 1554, and he wrote a grammar of the Tupi language and religious plays.

jose-de-antequera-y-castro.s: José de Antequera y Castro was a Panamanian-born judge of the Audiencia of Charcas sent to investigate the governor of Paraguay in 1721. He took over the governorship himself, backed by settlers who resented the Jesuits' control of Guaraní labour, and defied the viceroy,…

jose-de-escandon.s: José de Escandón was a Spanish military officer and colonial administrator commissioned by the viceroy of New Spain in 1746 to colonise the Gulf coast north of Tampico. From 1748 he founded more than twenty towns and missions between the Pánuco and Nueces rivers, creating the…

jose-fernando-de-abascal.s: José Fernando de Abascal was a Spanish officer who served as viceroy of Peru from 1806 to 1816. Making Lima the centre of royalist resistance to the Spanish American independence movements, he sent armies against the patriots in Upper Peru, Quito and Chile, where his troops…

jose-gaspar-rodriguez-de-francia.s: José Gaspar Rodríguez de Francia was a lawyer and theologian who led Paraguay after independence. He became dictator in 1814 and perpetual dictator in 1816, ruling as El Supremo until his death in 1840.

jose-hilario-lopez.s: José Hilario López was a Colombian general and Liberal politician who served as president of the Republic of New Granada from 1849 to 1853. His government carried out major liberal reforms, abolishing slavery from 1 January 1852, expelling the Jesuits and separating more of…

jose-joaquin-de-olmedo.s: José Joaquín de Olmedo was an Ecuadorian poet and statesman who wrote the ode La victoria de Junín in honour of Simón Bolívar. After Guayaquil threw off Spanish rule on 9 October 1820 he headed the government of the Free Province of Guayaquil until Bolívar annexed it to Gran…

jose-maria-barrera.s: José María Barrera was a Maya rebel leader in the Caste War of Yucatán. In 1850 he promoted the cult of the Speaking Cross at a cenote in eastern Yucatán, which gave the rebels divine guidance in war.

jose-miguel-carrera.s: José Miguel Carrera was a Chilean independence leader who seized power in a series of coups from 1811. He introduced a provisional constitution, the first national flag and the first press during the Patria Vieja.

jose-mujica.s: José Mujica was a former Tupamaro guerrilla, imprisoned for some thirteen years under military rule, who became president of Uruguay for the Frente Amplio from 2010 to 2015. His government legalised same-sex marriage and the production and sale of cannabis.

josef-friedrich-matthes.s: Josef Friedrich Matthes was a German journalist and Rhenish separatist who led the provisional government of the Rhenish Republic in Koblenz in 1923, alongside Hans Adam Dorten. The republic depended on the tolerance of French occupation forces and collapsed within months.

josef-terboven.s: Josef Terboven was a Nazi Party official and Gauleiter of Essen whom Hitler appointed Reich Commissioner for Norway in April 1940. He held real power over the occupied country from Oslo, working with Vidkun Quisling's Nasjonal Samling while repressing resistance through…

joseph-bonaparte.s: Joseph Bonaparte was the elder brother of Napoleon, who made him king of Naples in 1806. In Naples he abolished feudalism, closed monasteries and introduced French administration.

joseph-chatoyer.s: Joseph Chatoyer was paramount chief of the Garifuna, or Black Caribs, of Saint Vincent. He resisted British encroachment on Garifuna lands in the First Carib War and, allied with revolutionary France, led the Second Carib War of 1795.

joseph-de-saint-ovide-de-brouillan.s: Joseph de Saint-Ovide de Brouillan was a French officer who served in Acadia and Newfoundland before becoming governor of Île Royale, present-day Cape Breton Island, from 1717 to 1739. He oversaw the growth of Louisbourg as a fortified port and fishing centre, trading with…

joseph-dudley.s: Joseph Dudley was a Massachusetts-born colonial official, son of Governor Thomas Dudley. After the Massachusetts charter was revoked, he headed the interim government of New England from 1686 until Edmund Andros arrived.

joseph-frederick-wallet-desbarres.s: Joseph Frederick Wallet DesBarres was a Swiss-born military engineer and cartographer whose Atlantic Neptune charted the coasts of North America. In 1784 he became the first lieutenant governor of the new Colony of Cape Breton Island and founded Sydney as its capital in 1785.

joseph-nasi.s: Joseph Nasi was a Portuguese-born Jewish financier and diplomat who rose to great influence at the Ottoman court under Selim II. In 1566 the sultan made him duke of Naxos and the Archipelago after deposing its last Crispo duke, and he ruled the islands through a deputy.

joseph-francois-dupleix.s: Joseph François Dupleix was governor-general of French India at Pondicherry from 1742 to 1754. During the Carnatic wars he intervened in the succession disputes of the Carnatic and Hyderabad, raising sepoy armies and installing allied rulers, and briefly made France the…

josephine-de-beauharnais.s: Joséphine de Beauharnais was born at Trois-Îlets on Martinique into a planter family. Widowed when her husband Alexandre de Beauharnais was guillotined in 1794, she married Napoleon Bonaparte in 1796 and became Empress of the French in 1804, until their divorce in 1810.

josiah-zion-gumede.s: Josiah Zion Gumede was a Zimbabwean politician of Abel Muzorewa's United African National Council. Under the internal settlement he became the first and only president of Zimbabwe Rhodesia from June to December 1979, a largely ceremonial post.

josif-rajacic.s: Josif Rajačić was a Serbian Orthodox churchman, metropolitan of Karlovci from 1842. At the May Assembly of Sremski Karlovci in 1848 the Serbs of southern Hungary elected him patriarch and proclaimed the Serbian Vojvodina.

jovan-dragas.s: Jovan Dragaš was a Serbian nobleman, son of the sebastokrator Dejan and nephew of Stefan Dušan. After Dušan's death in 1355 he and his brother Konstantin Dragaš built an autonomous lordship in north-eastern Macedonia, around Kumanovo, Kyustendil and Strumica.

jozef-ostrowski.s: Józef Ostrowski was a Polish landowner and conservative politician who had sat in the Russian State Council. In 1917 he became one of the three members of the Regency Council of the Kingdom of Poland, alongside Archbishop Aleksander Kakowski and Prince Zdzisław Lubomirski.

juan-araneta.s: Juan Araneta was a sugar planter and revolutionary general from Bago on Negros Island in the Philippines. With Aniceto Lacson he led the rising of 5 November 1898 that drove out the Spanish garrison within days and set up the Republic of Negros.

juan-bautista-de-anza.s: Juan Bautista de Anza was a frontier officer of New Spain, born in Sonora, who led overland expeditions to Alta California in 1774 and 1775–1776, bringing the settlers who founded San Francisco. As governor of New Mexico from 1778 to 1787 he defeated the Comanche leader Cuerno…

juan-calfucura.s: Juan Calfucurá was a Mapuche leader who crossed from Araucanía to the Argentine pampas around 1835 and seized control of the Salinas Grandes salt flats. From there he built a powerful confederation of pampas peoples that raided the Argentine frontier for decades.

juan-carlos-i.s: Juan Carlos I was king of Spain from 1975 to 2014. Francisco Franco named him as his successor in 1969, but after Franco's death he backed the transition to democracy with Prime Minister Adolfo Suárez, leading to the constitution of 1978.

juan-de-garay.s: Juan de Garay was a Basque-born conquistador who served in Peru and Paraguay. From Asunción he founded Santa Fe in 1573 and refounded Buenos Aires in 1580, decades after Pedro de Mendoza's first settlement had been abandoned.

juan-de-onate.s: Juan de Oñate was a conquistador born in New Spain who led settlers, soldiers and Franciscans up the Camino Real in 1598 and founded the province of Santa Fe de Nuevo México. He became its first governor, but his brutal punishment of Acoma Pueblo in 1599 and costly failures…

juan-manuel-rodriguez.s: Juan Manuel Rodríguez was a Salvadoran independence leader who took part in the San Salvador uprising of 1811. After Central America left the Mexican Empire, he became the first head of state of El Salvador within the Federal Republic of Central America in 1824.

juan-mora-fernandez.s: Juan Mora Fernández was a Costa Rican teacher and politician who became the first head of state of Costa Rica within the Federal Republic of Central America, governing from 1824 to 1833. His administration kept the state out of the federal wars, encouraged coffee cultivation,…

juan-nepomuceno-almonte.s: Juan Nepomuceno Almonte was a Mexican soldier and diplomat, son of the independence leader José María Morelos. A conservative, he supported French intervention and headed the regency that governed in the name of the Second Mexican Empire from 1863 until Maximilian of Austria…

juan-nunez-i-de-lara.s: Juan Núñez I de Lara was a Castilian magnate of the powerful House of Lara. Through his marriage to Teresa Álvarez de Azagra he became lord of Albarracín, an independent lordship between Castile and Aragon.

juan-pablo-duarte.s: Juan Pablo Duarte was the leading founding father of the Dominican Republic. In 1838 he founded the secret society La Trinitaria to organise resistance to Haitian rule.

juan-peron.s: Juan Perón was an Argentine army officer who rose to power as labour minister after the 1943 coup and was elected president in 1946. With his wife Eva Perón he built a mass movement based on trade unions, industrialisation and social welfare.

juan-pio-de-tristan.s: Juan Pío de Tristán was a wealthy Arequipa landowner and royalist general who served as the last viceroy of Peru briefly in 1824, after the Battle of Ayacucho. He later accepted independence and became president of the South Peruvian Republic within Andrés de Santa Cruz's…

juan-rafael-mora-porras.s: Juan Rafael Mora Porras was a coffee merchant and president of Costa Rica from 1849 to 1859. He led the Central American coalition that defeated the American filibuster William Walker in Nicaragua in 1856 and 1857, and is honoured as a national hero.

juan-vicente-gomez.s: Juan Vicente Gómez was a soldier from the Andes who seized power in Venezuela in 1908 and ruled as dictator until his death in 1935. His regime crushed opposition, centralised the state and built a professional army.

jules-gros.s: Jules Gros was a French journalist and geographer whom adventurers in Paris named president for life of the Republic of Counani in 1886. The republic was proclaimed in territory disputed between France and Brazil in the Guiana region, but Gros never visited it, and the state…

julia-domna.s: Julia Domna was a Roman empress, daughter of the high priest of the sun god at Emesa in Syria. She married Septimius Severus and was the mother of the emperors Caracalla and Geta, and she accompanied Severus on his campaign in Britain against the Caledonians.

julian-grenier.s: Julian Grenier was lord of Sidon and Beaufort in the crusader Kingdom of Jerusalem. His raid into Mongol-held territory in 1260 provoked a Mongol attack that sacked Sidon.

julien-fedon.s: Julien Fédon was a free coloured planter of French descent on Grenada. Inspired by revolutionary France, he led the rebellion of 1795 to 1796, which won the support of enslaved people, held most of the island and killed the British lieutenant governor and other hostages.

julius-civilis.s: Julius Civilis was a Batavian noble and Roman auxiliary commander who led the Batavian revolt of 69 to 70 CE during the civil wars of the Year of the Four Emperors. Joined by the Cananefates, Frisii and Treveri, the rebels destroyed several Roman forts on the Rhine.

julius-echter-von-mespelbrunn.s: Julius Echter von Mespelbrunn was prince-bishop of Würzburg from 1573 to 1617. A leading figure of the Counter-Reformation, he forced Protestants to convert or leave, refounded the University of Würzburg in 1582 and built the Juliusspital hospital.

julius-sundblom.s: Julius Sundblom was a journalist and politician from the Åland Islands who led the movement for reunion with Sweden after Finnish independence. When the League of Nations awarded Åland to Finland with guaranteed autonomy in 1921, he became the first speaker of its parliament,…

julius-von-pflug.s: Julius von Pflug was a German humanist and Catholic theologian who sought reconciliation with the Lutherans and helped draft the Augsburg Interim of 1548. Elected bishop of Naumburg in 1541, he was kept out by the Lutheran Nicholas of Amsdorf until 1547.

junaid-khan.s: Junaid Khan was a Turkmen tribal leader of the Yomut who became the real power in the Khanate of Khiva from 1918. After the Red Army and the Young Khivans overthrew the khanate in 1920, he fought the Khorezm People's Soviet Republic and later Soviet rule as a leader of the…

juozas-ambrazevicius.s: Juozas Ambrazevičius was a Lithuanian literary scholar who served as acting prime minister of the Provisional Government of Lithuania in June to August 1941, after the uprising against Soviet rule at the start of the German invasion. The Germans dissolved the government, and…

jupiter-latiaris.s: Jupiter Latiaris was the form of Jupiter worshipped as the shared god of the Latin peoples at his sanctuary on the Alban Mount, now Monte Cavo, near the site of Alba Longa. His annual festival, the Feriae Latinae, gathered the Latin communities for a common sacrifice.

juqu-anzhou.s: Juqu Anzhou was a prince of the Northern Liang, brother of its last ruler Juqu Mujian. After Northern Wei conquered Northern Liang in 439, he and his brother Juqu Wuhui fled west and seized Gaochang in 442.

juqu-mujian.s: Juqu Mujian was the last ruler of the Northern Liang, one of the Sixteen Kingdoms in the Hexi Corridor, succeeding his father Juqu Mengxun in 433. Northern Wei captured his capital Guzang and took him prisoner in 439, completing its unification of northern China.

jurgen-wullenwever.s: Jürgen Wullenwever was a Lübeck merchant who rose to power as a popular Lutheran leader and became mayor in 1533. He tried to restore Lübeck's dominance of Baltic trade by intervening in the Danish succession, leading the city into the Count's Feud of 1534 to 1536.

juscelino-kubitschek.s: Juscelino Kubitschek was a doctor and politician, governor of Minas Gerais, who served as president of Brazil from 1956 to 1961. Promising 'fifty years in five', he pushed rapid industrialisation, road building and the motor industry.

justan-iii.s: Justan III was a ruler of the Justanid dynasty of Daylam in the mountains of northern Iran. After 864 he supported the Zaydi Alavid dynasty of Tabaristan, helping establish Shia Islam among the Daylamites.

justo-rufino-barrios.s: Justo Rufino Barrios was a Guatemalan general who led the Liberal Revolution of 1871 and ruled as president from 1873 to 1885. He expropriated church lands, expelled the Jesuits and built roads, railways and schools.

juvenal-habyarimana.s: Juvénal Habyarimana was a Rwandan army officer who seized power in a coup in 1973 and ruled a one-party state for over twenty years. The Rwandan Patriotic Front invaded in 1990, and he signed the Arusha Accords in 1993.

jayabaya.s: Jayabaya was king of Kediri in East Java in the mid 12th century. An inscription of 1135 records his victory over Janggala with the words Panjalu jayati, Panjalu is victorious, uniting the realm Airlangga had divided.

jinheung-of-silla.s: Jinheung was king of Silla from 540 to 576 and its greatest early conqueror. Allied with Baekje, he took the Han river valley from Goguryeo and then seized it from Baekje in 553, gaining access to the Yellow Sea.

john-ii-of-aragon.s: John II was King of Navarre by marriage from 1425 and King of Aragon from 1458 until his death. His conflict with his son Charles of Viana and with the Catalan institutions led to the Catalan Civil War of 1462 to 1472, which he eventually won.

jun-of-gojoseon.s: Jun was the last king of the Gija line of Gojoseon in northern Korea, according to Chinese and Korean historical tradition. Around 194 BCE he was overthrown by Wiman, a refugee from the Chinese state of Yan whom he had employed to guard his frontier.

john-lambton-1st-earl-of-durham.s: John Lambton, 1st Earl of Durham, was a British Whig statesman sent as governor-general of British North America after the rebellions of 1837–1838. His Report on the Affairs of British North America of 1839 recommended uniting Upper and Lower Canada, partly to assimilate…

james-bruce-8th-earl-of-elgin.s: James Bruce, 8th Earl of Elgin, was a British colonial administrator who served as governor-general of the Province of Canada from 1847 to 1854. By signing the Rebellion Losses Bill in 1849 despite riots that burned the parliament in Montreal, he confirmed responsible government.

judicial-committee-of-the-privy-council.n: Judicial Committee of the Privy Council
judicial-committee-of-the-privy-council.s: The Judicial Committee of the Privy Council, set up in London in 1833, served as the final court of appeal for British colonies and dominions. Its rulings settled many imperial disputes, among them Sobhuza II's unsuccessful land case from Swaziland in 1926 and the 1927 award…

joanna-i-of-naples.s: Joanna I was queen of Naples and countess of Provence from 1343 to 1382. Her reign was troubled by the murder of her first husband and wars with Hungary.

jai-singh-ii.s: Jai Singh II was the Kachhwaha raja of Amber in Rajasthan from 1699 to 1743 and a leading noble of the late Mughal Empire. In 1727 he founded the new capital of Jaipur, laid out on a grid plan.

jamshid-bin-abdullah.s: Jamshid bin Abdullah was the last sultan of Zanzibar. He succeeded his father in July 1963 and reigned as constitutional monarch when Zanzibar became independent in December 1963, but was overthrown by the Zanzibar Revolution of January 1964, which created the People's…
